value: Currency with the public, demand deposits and 'other' deposits with the RBI
reasoning: Narrow money M1 is defined as currency with the public plus demand deposits with the banking system plus other deposits with the Reserve Bank; bankers' deposits with the Reserve Bank are part of reserve money and are deliberately excluded, since counting them would double-count the base of the deposits already included.

value: Exports rise, imports fall, and domestic inflation rises
reasoning: A weaker currency makes home goods cheaper for foreigners and foreign goods dearer at home, so exports expand and imports contract; because imported inputs and fuel now cost more in rupees, the cost push raises domestic inflation.

value: Customs duties
reasoning: Basic customs duty on imports was expressly kept outside the Goods and Services Tax and continues to be levied alongside it, whereas central excise duty and service tax were folded into GST at the outset. Petroleum products sit within the constitutional scope of GST even though the Council has not yet notified the date from which the levy will apply to them.

value: Minimum potential energy at the lowest, central position
reasoning: Gravitational potential energy depends on height, so the bob has least potential energy where it hangs lowest, which is the mean position directly below the point of suspension, and most at the extreme positions where it is raised highest.

value: Stainless steel
reasoning: Sound travels fastest where the medium is most rigid and least compressible, so its speed is greatest in solids, less in liquids and least in gases; among these, steel carries sound at nearly 6,000 metres per second against about 1,500 in water and only a few hundred in oxygen, and it is stiffer than glass.

value: Force is maximum when velocity and magnetic field are perpendicular
reasoning: The magnetic force on a moving charge is qvB sine of the angle between the velocity and the field, so it peaks when that angle is a right angle and vanishes when the two are parallel or antiparallel.

value: Fahrenheit equals nine-fifths of Celsius plus 32
reasoning: There are 180 Fahrenheit degrees between the ice and steam points against 100 Celsius degrees, giving the ratio nine-fifths, and the ice point sits at 32 on the Fahrenheit scale, which fixes the additive constant.

value: It slows down and bends towards the normal
reasoning: A denser medium has a higher refractive index, in which light travels more slowly, and by Snell's law the reduced speed makes the ray bend towards the normal on entering.

value: Burning of a candle
reasoning: A burning candle shows both changes at once: the wax melts and vaporises, which is reversible and physical, while the vapour then burns in air to form carbon dioxide and water, which is an irreversible chemical change. Freezing is purely physical, and rusting is purely chemical.

value: Diamond is hard while graphite is smooth and slippery
reasoning: Both are allotropes of carbon but their structures differ: diamond is a rigid three-dimensional network of covalent bonds and so is extremely hard, whereas graphite is built of layers held together by weak forces that slide over one another, making it soft, slippery and, because of its free electrons, a conductor of electricity.

value: Sugar
reasoning: Sugar is sucrose, a single substance whose elements are combined chemically in a fixed proportion, whereas air, milk and tea are mixtures whose components are present in variable proportions and are not chemically bonded.
Of the elements known today, the first 94 occur in nature, some like neptunium and plutonium only in traces, while everything beyond them exists solely as a product of artificial synthesis.

value: The claim that oxalic acid is found in tamarind paste
reasoning: Tamarind owes its sourness to tartaric acid; oxalic acid is characteristic of tomato and spinach. Gastric juice does contain hydrochloric acid, vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid, and citrus fruits carry both citric and ascorbic acid.

value: Mitochondria respiration, chloroplast photosynthesis, ribosome protein synthesis, rough ER transport of proteins
reasoning: Mitochondria release energy by oxidising food and chloroplasts trap light to make it, ribosomes assemble amino acids into proteins, and the rough endoplasmic reticulum, studded with those ribosomes, channels the proteins to their destinations.

value: Tapeworm
reasoning: A cell wall is absent in animals, and the tapeworm is an animal; bacteria have a peptidoglycan wall, diatoms a silica shell and mushrooms, being fungi, a wall of chitin.

value: Transpiration pull together with cohesion and adhesion
reasoning: Evaporation from the leaves creates a suction, the transpiration pull, which is transmitted down an unbroken water column held together by cohesion between water molecules and held to the narrow xylem walls by adhesion.

value: Energy flow is unidirectional and nutrient flow is cyclic
reasoning: Energy enters as sunlight and is progressively lost as heat at each trophic level, so it can never be reused and moves only one way; nutrients, being matter, are returned to the soil by decomposers and circulate again through the biogeochemical cycles.

value: Rhizopus
reasoning: Rhizopus, the bread mould, is a fungus that secretes enzymes onto dead organic matter and absorbs the digested nutrients, which is saprophytic nutrition; Cuscuta is a parasite and Spirogyra and grass are autotrophs.

value: Nucellus
reasoning: The nucellus is the sporophytic tissue of the ovule and so carries the diploid number of chromosomes, whereas the egg, synergids and antipodals are all cells of the embryo sac formed from the haploid megaspore.

value: Capture of Torna, annexation of Javli, attack on Afzal Khan, attack on Shaista Khan
reasoning: Shivaji's career opens with the seizure of Torna in the mid-1640s, followed by the annexation of Javli in 1656, the killing of Afzal Khan at Pratapgarh in 1659 and the night raid on Shaista Khan at Poona in 1663.

value: Subhas Chandra Bose
reasoning: The Indian Struggle was written by Subhas Chandra Bose during his years in Europe as his own account of the national movement, its later edition carrying the story down to 1942.

value: Andal
reasoning: The three women among the sixty-three Nayanars, who were devotees of Shiva, are Karaikkal Ammaiyar, Mangayarkkarasiyar and Isaignaniyar; Andal belongs to the Alvars, the Tamil devotees of Vishnu.

value: Nattar paired with 'male serpent deity'
reasoning: In Chola-period south India the nattar were the assembly of landholders of the nadu, a territorial unit, not a deity. The other pairings hold: a yupa is the sacrificial post of Vedic ritual and a viragal is the Tamil hero stone raised for a warrior who died in battle.

value: Uttar Pradesh
reasoning: The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh, an early stone temple of the Gupta age famous for its Sheshashayi Vishnu panel, stands in Lalitpur district of Uttar Pradesh.

value: Only the statement about the raised left leg in bhujangatrasita
reasoning: In the Chola Nataraja the right leg presses down on the dwarf Apasmara, the demon of ignorance, while it is the raised left leg in bhujangatrasita that stands for tirobhava, the kicking away of the veil of illusion; the main right hand is held in abhaya mudra granting assurance, the damaru being carried in an upper hand.

value: Alphabetical rotation of the chairmanship, and the ASEAN motto
reasoning: Under the ASEAN Charter the chairmanship rotates annually in the alphabetical order of the members' English names, so no vote is taken, and the grouping's motto is One Vision, One Identity, One Community. ASEAN Day falls on 8 August, the date of the Bangkok Declaration of 1967, not 12 August.

value: Joint Centre-State responsibility, the FCI's procurement and transport role, and additional commodities supplied by some States
reasoning: The Public Distribution System is run jointly by the Centre and the States, with the Food Corporation of India handling procurement, storage, transport and bulk allocation, and several States adding pulses, edible oil, iodised salt and similar items at their fair price shops. Identifying eligible families, however, is an operational task left to the State governments alone.

value: Equity, sustainability and productivity
reasoning: Human development rests on four pillars — equity, sustainability, productivity and empowerment; security is a concern of the related idea of human security but is not one of those four, so the listed set is correct except for it.

value: Introduction of the World Wide Web dated to 1995
reasoning: The World Wide Web was devised by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN and released at the start of the 1990s, in 1991, not 1995. Telstar, the first active communications satellite, went up in 1962, SWIFT began operating in 1977 and the round-the-world fibre-optic link was completed in 1997.

value: Saline soil
reasoning: Soils charged with sodium, potassium and magnesium salts, sandy to loamy in texture and infertile, are the saline or usar soils; they occur in arid western Gujarat and in the coastal deltas of the east and the Sundarbans, where seawater ingress and poor drainage concentrate the salts.
